abstract: The AI boom is usually discussed as a contest over models, chips, and productivity. This column argues that it is also a large physical infrastructure and credit cycle. The policy priority is not to call the peak, but to measure who owns the assets, who owes the debt, and where contingent obligations will land if demand disappoints.
abstract_zh: 人工智能热潮通常被讨论为一场围绕模型、芯片和生产率的竞赛。本专栏认为，它同时也是一场规模庞大的实体基础设施与信贷周期。政策优先事项不是判断峰值何时到来，而是衡量谁拥有这些资产、谁背负债务，以及如果需求令人失望，或有负债将落在何处。
title: Financing the AI buildout before the risks go off balance sheet
title_zh: 在为风险转出资产负债表之前为人工智能建设融资

abstract: High public debt in several euro-area countries has renewed the debate over a central question: can fiscal pressures in one member state affect inflation expectations elsewhere by constraining the ECB? This column uses a randomised information experiment with German firms to show that the answer depends on trust in the central bank. Pessimistic debt projections for France, Italy, and Spain raise the three-year inflation expectations of firms that distrust the ECB, while high-trust firms do not react. By contrast, a €500 billion German debt package leaves inflation expectations unchanged.
abstract_zh: 几个欧元区国家的高公共债务重新引发了对一个核心问题的辩论：一个成员国的财政压力能否通过约束欧洲央行来影响其他地区的通胀预期？本专栏利用一项针对德国企业的随机信息实验表明，答案取决于对中央银行的信任。对法国、意大利和西班牙的悲观债务预测，会提高那些不信任欧洲央行的企业的三年期通胀预期，而高信任度的企业则没有反应。相比之下，一项5000亿欧元的德国债务计划并未使通胀预期发生变化。
authors: Francesco Bianchi, Renato Faccini, Leonardo Melosi, Nils Wehrhöfer
title: Your debt, my inflation: The role of trust in the ECB
title_zh: 你的债务，我的通胀：信任在欧洲央行中的作用
